d: Paired mucus-secreting greater vestibular glands at about 4 and 8 o'clock in the vestibule that lubricate the introitus; a blocked duct forms a cyst or abscess.
Vaginal squamous cells so coated with Gardnerella and other bacteria that their borders look stippled; more than 20% of epithelial cells is an Amsel criterion for bacterial vaginosis.
A chronic T-cell-mediated vulvar dermatosis of thin, white, parchment-like skin in a figure-of-eight around the vulva and anus; it spares the vagina and carries a small cancer risk.
The HPV-independent vulvar precursor, with atypia confined to the basal layer, aberrant p53 staining and absent or patchy p16; it arises in lichen sclerosus and leads to keratinizing carcinoma.
An intraepithelial adenocarcinoma of the vulva with large pale PAS-positive, CK7-positive cells in the epidermis; unlike breast Paget disease, it usually has no underlying carcinoma.
The botryoid form of embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma: a grape-like vaginal mass in girls under 5, with small round blue cells in a cambium layer that stain for desmin and myogenin.

Inflammation of the cervix, most often from chlamydia or gonorrhea, with mucopurulent discharge from the os, postcoital bleeding and a friable cervix; untreated infection can ascend to cause pelvic inflammatory disease.
